column1: # Every function of the node source that reads the bytes of a secret (rule E2 of the egress
# policy, docs/egress-policy.md). `scripts/secret-access.sh --check` compares the first three
# columns with the source and fails when a function is missing here or no longer exists.
# Columns, separated by tabs: file, function, uses of `expose_secret` in it (for
# protocol/src/secret.rs: uses of the private fields), use, note.
# use: K1 record ciphertext, K2 seal to a verified peer, K3 TLS connection to a provider,
# K4 vault value of `release`, K5 TLS connection to the log store, in-node (the result stays
# inside the node or is a signature, a ciphertext or a public key), declassify (the result
# leaves in the clear and is one of the declassified values of docs/egress-policy.md section 4).

column5: the length of a request body the node assembled, for the Content-Length of the request to the provider
writes a secret header value and a secret body into the request that goes to the provider over TLS

signs a request to the log store with AWS Signature Version 4: the session token of the operator is one of the signed headers, and its secret access key is the key of the HMAC chain. What leaves is the signature, in the request that goes to the log store over TLS. Neither value is a secret of an account
writes the session token of the operator into a header of the request that goes to the log store over TLS
encodes 32 random bytes as the verifier text: the result is a secret
the S256 challenge of the verifier, part of the authorization address
parses the opened plaintext of a token record: the result is a secret
a token response becomes the plaintext of a record: the result is a secret
the refresh rule over two secrets: the result is a secret
the reconnect rule over two secrets: the result is a secret
the refresh token for a token request: the result is a secret
the token for a revocation request: the result is a secret
the token and the header value of a forward request: both results are secrets
the client id a record holds, for a token or revocation request: the result is a secret
the public fields of rule E4: the listed leaves, the time the token was obtained, one bit for the refresh token, or the refusal response_withheld
serializes the plaintext for record::seal: the bytes leave as the ciphertext of a record
the length of a value, for the size of the buffer the form body is written into
writes the secret values into the form body of a token or revocation request: the body is a secret
writes the secret values into the JSON body of a token request: the body is a secret
the HTTP Basic header value of a token or revocation request: the result is a secret
of an accepted token response nothing: it stays a secret. Of a refused one the HTTP status and one word of the closed vocabulary of rule E5
the encoded forms of a credential for the search: each form is a secret
one bit: whether bytes a provider sent hold a credential (the refusal response_withheld)
two random values become the private keys of the node
parses a vault plaintext and takes one field, or computes the TOTP code of the seed: the result is a secret
a vault value becomes part of the response of release, after its log entry
the public parts of a grant or a revoke command (user_id, challenge, sign_pk, log_pk, custody, not_after_ms). The user key becomes a secret
user keys go into the payload of a delegation transfer: the payload is a secret
signs the transfer payload and seals it to the sealing key of the verified peer
the public parts of the grants of a transfer (user_id, sign_pk, log_pk, custody, not_after_ms). The user keys become secrets
the key material of the HPKE seal of a log entry
decrypts a record with the user key: the plaintext is a secret
encrypts a secret plaintext under a key derived from the user key
the accessor itself: its callers are the lines above
creates a secret in place from the random source
copies a key into another secret
overwrites the bytes with zeros
the signing public key of the node
the sealing public key of the node
an Ed25519 signature of the node over a body
an Ed25519 signature of the node over a transfer payload
opens an HPKE seal made to the node: the plaintext is a secret
